traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 206 Ebenaceae: trees or shrubs, the wood often hard and black (ebony); leaves alternate, rarely opposite, entire; no stipules; flowers mostly of one sex, often on separate plants (persimmons); calyx 3- to 6-lobed, persisting and often growing in fruit; corolla 3- to 7-lobed; stamens 2 to 4 times the corolla lobes; ovary superior; fruit a more or less juicy berry.

traits.inflorescence.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 302, 303, family Ebenaceae: inflorescence cyme, axillary, usually; read as {"cyme": "usually"}.

traits.flowering_position.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 302, 303, family Ebenaceae: flowering position lateral, usually; read as {"lateral": "usually"}.
